clauses.reason: Terminated by supersession or revocation. EO 10480 (Dwight D. Eisenhower, August 14, 1953; 18 FR 4939), held Federal Register text, section 607 reads "The following are superseded or revoked:" and lists "Executive Order No. 10359 of June 9 1962 (17 F. R. 5269)." The section does not say which of the two (superseded or revoked) applies to each listed order; either ends the order's force. EO 10480 states no later effective date, so the signing date August 14, 1953 is the end date. Section 1 ends with the order. The listing prints the date of EO 10359 as "June 9 1962", an obvious misprint of 1952 in the transcription; the number and the Federal Register citation identify the order.

research_rationale:
EO 10359 (June 9, 1952, Harry S. Truman; 17 FR 5269), amending EO 10161 with respect to certain plant fibers, is read in full in the held Federal Register text. Section 1 amends sections 303, 307, 310(b) and 311(b) of EO 10161 to read as the order prints them (the quoted sections concern the Defense Materials Procurement Administrator's functions and loans and the certificates of essentiality for loans, with a role for the Secretary of Agriculture over plant fibers other than abaca); section 2 gives the order precedence over inconsistent prior orders and keeps other actions in effect. The order has no stated term. EO 10480 (August 14, 1953), held Federal Register text, lists it in section 607 among orders "superseded or revoked". That is the first end for both rows.

savings.reason: EO 10480 section 606 keeps in effect actions relating to functions it affects, except as inconsistent with it. Certificates of essentiality and loans made under the amended sections before August 14, 1953 are acts under them, not commands of this order; no held source shows the plant-fibre provisions continuing after that date, which is a disclosed qualification, not a finding.
